## Research Across Borders for Fairer Working Lives

ÇAHSPAR is an independent academic association founded in Türkiye with an international research mission in working life and social policy. We bring together researchers across disciplines, institutions and countries to examine how societies organise work, distribute opportunities and protect people throughout their lives.

Our mission is to develop comparative knowledge, international research partnerships and evidence that can inform decent work, inclusive social protection and more equitable societies. We connect labour economics and industrial relations with social policy, sociology, education, migration studies and research on technological and environmental change.

## A Global Research Horizon

Our research ambition extends across the **193 Member States of the United Nations**. This defines the geographical horizon of our agenda; individual studies will specify their country coverage, data availability and research partnerships.

For regional comparisons, we use the ILO’s five broad geographical regions as a reference:

- **Africa**
- **Americas**
- **Arab States**
- **Asia and the Pacific**
- **Europe and Central Asia**

These are analytical groupings rather than five continents. Regional and country studies will follow the relevant ILO country groupings and document any differences in the coverage of their data sources. The UN membership count and the coverage of ILO statistical datasets serve different purposes and need not coincide.

Our approach brings regional expertise into conversation with global analysis. We seek to understand both shared pressures and the institutional, historical and social conditions that make policy outcomes differ across countries.

## A Comparative Research Agenda

We aim to investigate the quality and security of employment, collective representation, social protection, poverty and inequality, gender and care, migration, youth transitions, skills, social entrepreneurship and the future of work.

Particular attention goes to questions that cross national boundaries: how global production networks shape working conditions; how digitalisation redistributes opportunity and risk; how migration connects labour markets and welfare systems; and how climate transitions can be made socially just.

Comparative research requires attention to context. We combine quantitative and qualitative approaches, assess the comparability of indicators and examine whose experiences are missing from available evidence. Policy learning should explain why an intervention works, for whom and under which conditions before considering its relevance elsewhere.

## International Cooperation and Knowledge Exchange

We seek sustained collaboration with international associations in labour and social policy, universities, research centres, professional networks, civil society organisations and workers’ and employers’ organisations.

Our partnership agenda includes joint studies, international project consortia, co-authored publications, conferences, workshops, researcher exchanges and mentoring. We aim to develop equitable partnerships in which researchers from different regions help define the questions, methods and interpretation of findings.

We follow research, statistics and policy publications from the ILO, other United Nations bodies and international organisations, alongside scholarly journals and specialist research networks. Critical synthesis of this literature will help identify emerging debates, gaps in evidence and opportunities for collaborative projects.

## Connecting Türkiye with Global Scholarship

Founded by nine academics, ÇAHSPAR draws on Türkiye’s scholarship in labour economics, industrial relations and social policy while building an international community open to researchers across the world.

We aim to increase the international visibility of research from Türkiye through comparative studies, joint publications, international conferences and participation in research networks. Türkiye’s experience can contribute to global debates on employment, welfare, migration and social transformation, while international collaboration can deepen research and policy discussion within Türkiye.

Knowledge exchange is reciprocal. We seek to make research from different regions more accessible to one another and to create opportunities for scholars whose work is underrepresented in international debate.

## Supporting the Next Generation

Early-career researchers and doctoral students are central to our long-term vision. We aim to connect them with international collaborators, methodological learning, constructive peer feedback and opportunities to contribute to joint research and publications.

Our research groups provide a thematic basis for collaboration across career stages and geographical boundaries. Scientific quality, fair recognition of contributions and openness to different research traditions guide this work.

## From Evidence to Public Value

Our ambition is to make research useful beyond the university. Through policy briefs, comparative reports, academic publications and dialogue with practitioners, we aim to connect robust evidence with decisions affecting working conditions, social security, equality and wellbeing.

We value scientific independence, research ethics, transparent methods and responsible use of data. We seek accessible communication without losing the complexity of the evidence or overstating what a study can establish.

**Our vision is an international research community that advances knowledge across borders and contributes to dignified work and social justice worldwide.**
